title: a ticket cast on a far box carries its berths to the commons
intention: cast_ticket copies every berth a ticket cites (sorted_berth, and an intent_berth that is a file) into the commons at berths/<skill>/<name>. read_berth falls back to that copy when the path does not resolve on this box. So a ticket cast on any box crosses BUILDME on the home box with no hand copy.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendelllinux, relayed verbatim: BUILDME for 1029d5146152 and 99258e9bbdb1 was refused '[buildme_rides_the_sorted] sorted berth readable (expected: True, actual: False)'. The berths were fired on akienasus and sit in its instance-space; the crossing needed an scp of each berth.
traces_to: the three roots (CLAUDE.md: if losing it loses knowledge, it's commons) and Law 8 (the gate's evidence must be readable where the gate runs).
how: At cast, after _berth_lacks passes, write each cited berth's bytes through the artifact door to <CairnCommons>/berths/<skill>/<name>. read_berth gains a third candidate, the commons address, after the reviewed address. Red-first proof against a scratch commons.

clauses.claim: cast_ticket over a doc whose sorted_berth and intent_berth are files writes a byte-identical copy of each at <commons>/berths/<skill>/<basename>
read_berth over a berth path that does not exist on this box returns the commons copy's document
a 'none, because' intent_berth writes no copy, and the cast is otherwise unchanged

decisions.text: D1: cast_ticket writes each cited berth file through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write to <CairnCommons>/berths/<parent dir name>/<basename>, verb 'cast', after _berth_lacks passes and before the ticket write.
D2: read_berth tries <CairnCommons>/berths/<parent name>/<name> after reviewed_address.
D3: a red-first proof, one tooth per clause, casting into a scratch commons.

measured.saw: [buildme_rides_the_sorted] sorted berth readable (expected: True, actual: False)
measured.how: sail.py cross 1029d5146152 and 99258e9bbdb1 on akiendelllinux, berths fired on akienasus (relayed by the orchestrator)
